blocks.text: LIMOGES, France — The town hall in the French city of Limoges was on fire on Saturday, authorities said, after a group attacked the building during unrest that broke out after cost-of-living protests. The blaze had spread to one wing of the 143-year-old building and reached the roof, a witness told AFP. Firefighters were deployed to try to prevent the flames consuming the entire town hall. READ: Tens of thousands expected in Paris for high school protests Nearby, as hundreds of people watched the blaze, a municipal employee was seen in tears, comforted by a local councillor.
